title: Claude Code co-wrote 154 of the first 157 commits of my turn-based browser RPG
author: Majestic_Sun3360
selftext:
Hey, I'm the dev of Ten Thousand Rebirths. 

It's a turn-based text RPG that runs in the browser, set in the cultivation genre (Chinese and Korean martial arts stories). It's free to play and has a premium currency you can buy. I can code a bit (Python, C# and Lua from years of writing WoW addons), but I'd never built anything new from scratch before. In my day job I'm a project lead, and directing Claude turned out to be pretty close to that. I write down what I want and I decide what goes live.

For balance, Claude wrote a fight simulator. That's how I found out the final boss had a 0% win rate over 300 simulated fights. Now every balance change goes through the sim before it ships.

The art is from ChatGPT and Gemini. For the roughly 70 enemy portraits I generated sprite sheets with ten enemies each instead of single images, because the style stayed more consistent that way. A 40-line script cuts the sheets into single portraits.

The whole game runs on one Cloudflare Worker with SQLite, and the client is a single HTML file. Fights are calculated on the server with seeded RNG and the browser only replays the log.

Claude also makes my devlog. It reads the git history and writes the script. The voice is from ElevenLabs and the footage is real screen recordings. Episode 1: https://youtu.be/5fl_3tdKDWE

My problem right now is getting people to stay. In the two days after my first Reddit post about 50 people signed up and only 3 stayed longer than five minutes. Since I gave new accounts a full day of turns it's 10 out of 18, which is better but still not great. Has anyone here used AI to figure out where players drop off? I'd also take any ideas on how a text game can hook people in the first few minutes.

Play it here: https://tenthousandrebirths.com/?ref=aigamedev

replies.author: Majestic_Sun3360
replies.body:
Okay, I really like the way it works. But I am generally interested in how the AI is prompted and where it runs to create the story. It was not clear to me that I would start a DnD campaign. But I really like the way it generates pictures fitting the situation and that the 4 choices are each pretty different. Very nicely done.  
Although the Wall of text can be intimidating for people playing "a game". But if you tell them it is DnD it should be fine.

replies.author: jleechanworldai
replies.body:
At least for me for your game it seems too complicated and I don't feel inclined to invest more time to learn it. The game maybe needs less info and a tutorial. You can see how i tried to keep mine a bit simpler.

I like the first screen choosing my character but second screen makes me not feel like investing more time. In the world of infinite AI games/distractions attention is very important to manage.

This is the second screen and feels kinda complicated to learn.

https://i.redd.it/d3krx4pwkf3i1.png

replies.author: Majestic_Sun3360
replies.body: Thank you for the input, I am fixing stuff immediately!

replies.author: jleechanworldai
replies.body: I like the concept though. I was excited to initially play it but I churned with the complexity

comments.author: IndiBestEngineer
comments.body: the "too complicated" comments are the same thing i got on mine. a stranger's detailed notes said upgrades took dozens of clicks because there were too many currencies, and he stopped around the third universe. i'd try hiding half the systems for the first 10 minutes and see where people stop
